name: SiteHeader
label: Site header
description: A site's sticky top bar of section pills and mega menus, folding to a drawer when the pills no longer fit or below a set breakpoint.

props.name: brand
props.description:
The brand at the bar's start, usually a logo linking home. Rendered as
given, so it carries its own link.

props.name: sections
props.description: The site's top-level sections, in order.

props.name: currentHref
props.description: The path of the page being viewed, used to mark the current section, row and drawer item.

props.name: actions
props.description: Controls at the bar's end that stay at every width, such as a search button; `condensedActions`, when given, stand in for them on the condensed step.

props.name: condensedActions
props.description:
The same controls drawn narrower, such as an icon-only CommandPaletteTrigger and a
`cycle` ThemeToggle. When the full row stops fitting, these take the place of
`actions` (the header adds `ds-site-header--condensed`), and the pills fold to the
menu button only when the condensed row does not fit either. Without it the
header folds as soon as the full row stops fitting.

props.name: wideActions
props.description:
Controls at the bar's end that show only while the pills fit, such as a
Get started button. Once the bar folds to its menu button they leave it; put
their drawer twin in `drawerFooter`.

props.name: drawerFooter
props.description: Content for the drawer's footer, such as the controls `wideActions` holds in the bar. It shows on the drawer's first level only: a level the reader drilled into leaves it out.

props.name: drawerHeader
props.description: Content above the drawer's first level of rows, such as a search field. It leaves when the reader drills in.

props.name: drawerEntries
props.description:
More of the drawer's first level, after the sections: rows and sections
of DrillMenu entries, such as a row that drills into a site's resources
or a group of settings that drill into their choices. Plain rows ahead
of the first section join the sections' own list, with no gap; a
section starts a group of its own.

props.name: drawerOpen
props.description: Whether the folded bar's drawer is open, for a host that owns that state. Pair with `onDrawerOpenChange`.

props.name: defaultDrawerOpen
props.description: Whether the drawer starts open, when the header owns its state.

props.name: onDrawerOpenChange
props.description: Called when the drawer opens or closes, controlled or not.

props.name: initialFold
props.description:
Where the bar folds before it has measured itself: on the first frame,
which a server-rendered page shows before its script runs. Below this
breakpoint (`tablet` or the wider `mid`) the bar starts folded by CSS
alone, so a phone never sees the pills overflow; the measurement takes
over once the script runs. Pick the step nearest where the pills stop
fitting, or `never` for a bar that fits at every width. Defaults to
`foldBelow` when that is set, so a bar told to fold at a step starts
folded there too and never shifts when its script runs.

props.name: foldBelow
props.description:
Fold the bar into its menu at or below this breakpoint even when the
pills would fit (`tablet` is 959px and below, `mid` 1279px), for a site
whose sidebar of pages leaves the page there: the menu then carries the
pages (each section's `drawerItems`), so the reader always has one way
in. Leave it out to fold only when the row runs out of room.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Whether the header sticks to the top of the viewport over a progressive
blur. Off, it scrolls away with the page and draws no blur.

props.name: tintAfter
props.description:
How far, in pixels, the page scrolls before the page-surface tint fades
in over the sticky header's blur. By default it arrives with the first
pixel of scroll, at the fast step, so page text never slides up under a
clear bar.

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
The component every link renders through, so a router's link (Next.js
`Link`) navigates without a reload. Falls back to the nearest
`LinkProvider`, then `<a>`.

props.name: navLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the section links' `<nav>` landmark.

props.name: drawerOpenLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the menu button that opens the drawer.

props.name: drawerTitle
props.description:
The drawer's title, naming the dialog. Shown at its top when there is no
`brand`; with one, the brand takes its place and the title is read only
by assistive tech.

props.name: drawerCloseLabel
props.description: The accessible name of the drawer's close button.

props.name: drawerBackLabel
props.description:
The drawer's back row's accessible name, given the title of the level it
returns to, for a site in another language. The drill menu's own default.

props.name: drawerOverviewLabel
props.description:
The text of the overview row a drilled level opens with when its row has
a page of its own, given that row's label, for a site in another
language. The drill menu's own default.

props.name: width
props.description:
How wide the bar's contents run, read from the shell recipe's width
axis. `contained` centres them in the contained width (1440px, or the
nearest `--ds-shell-contained-width`) with the side gutter, lining up
with a contained page below; `full` runs them edge to edge, the gutter
aside. Leave it out and the bar fills whatever box the host gives it,
with no gutter of its own; inside a SiteLayout it follows the layout's
`headerWidth` instead.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes on the `<header>`.

DrillMenuEntry.description: An entry on a level: a row, or a section of rows.

DrillMenuSection.description:
A group of rows under an optional heading: one level's resources or
settings, say, set apart from the rows above it.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.

MegaMenuItem.description: One link row in a mega menu: a page and the line that says what is on it.

MegaMenuShowcase.description: The featured card beside a mega menu's link grid: one link that is the whole card.

SiteHeaderDrawerItem.description:
A page in a section's drawer level. One with `items` drills into a level
of its own (a category of pages), opening with an overview row to `href`.

SiteHeaderSection.description: One top-level section of the site: a pill in the bar, a row in the drawer.

keys.note: Focusing a section opens its panel, Arrow Down moves into it, and Escape closes it.
